newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn rejects Fischler plan to cut farm spending.
newsitem.headline: Bonn rejects Fischler plan to cut farm spending.

text.p: German farm minister Jochen Borchert in a statement on Thursday rejected plans by European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler to cut farmers' compensatory payments at upcoming EU talks.
"There won't be a consensus on such plans because they could threaten the survival of many farms in Germany and other EU member states," the statement said.

Fischler, who is due to present a plan for the 1997/98 (July/June) farm price package next week, is expected to suggest keeping farm prices stable but to cut compensatory payments by 1.4 billion Ecus.
The cuts would be made to cereals and oilseeds aid as well as payments in return for land set-aside.
Borchert said Fischler's proposal would run contrary to promises made in the EU's 1992 farm reform package which said the compensatory payments would be permanent.
Fischler's move would question the very existence of a Common Agricultural Policy in the EU at a time when farmers needed clear assurances of future support from the EU, Borchert said.
